description: Lore every realm tells (the frontier, Darkness Falls, the old world), from Living Server, rewritten.

lines.text: Legion keeps a court down there like a king. Princes, high lords, dukes, earls, marquises, and every demon knows its rank.
Three demon princes sit under Legion, and each one of them would wipe a careless group.
Prince Abdin, Prince Asmoien, Prince Ba'alorien. Say them three times and see who shows up.
I like to think Grand Chancellor Adremal keeps Legion's books. Even demons need clerks.
Field Marshal Nebir drills Legion's army, or so the old raiders say.
Heard the Chthonic Knights stop most raids long before anyone sees Legion.
Word is Legion can send people straight into Behemoth's room, and that is the end of your evening.
Even Legion has a chamberlain. Somebody has to sweep the floors.
I have walked past the dukes so often I know them by name. Alloc, Aypol, Bimure, old neighbours.
The earls down there have names no Bard could rhyme. Zh'alzhak, Glassalab, Ipostian, I ask you.
Behemoth cannot be killed. Every guild that tried says the same, nothing sticks to him.
I think Behemoth is not a monster at all, he is a lock, and nobody has found the key.
A bright seal is worth more than a dull one, even the imps know that.
I like to think the demons were down there ages before any of us found the portal.
They say the demons crawled up out of the deep once the three realms went to war with each other.
Grand Summoner Govannon starts the fight as an Elf and finishes it as a demon. Nobody knows which one is the real him.
Aidon the Archwizard sits in the Hall of the Corrupt on the way down to the summoners, and nobody can say whose side he is on.
Three summoners and their sidhe guards, all in one hall. Someone planned that.
The summoners in that hall keep calling something. Nobody I know has asked them what.
I heard the Summoner's Hall was a sidhe place before Legion's lot moved in.
I think the tunnels and the Summoner's Hall are one plan. Someone is calling the dead from all three realms at once.
The dead in the tunnels serve a power nobody has named, and I do not think it is Legion.
While three realms fight over keeps, something is digging under all of us. Funny how that goes.
Every realm found tunnels under its own frontier, and every realm swears it found them first.
I followed a tunnel until my torch ran low, and it went further than any map said.
Wolf, stone or glimmer, which dragon is oldest? Every realm says its own.
Three realms, three dragons. A wolf, a stone and a glimmer, and every realm thinks theirs is the worst.
Heard the dragons have never met. Probably for the best, one of them would eat the other two.
I think the three dragons are kin, scattered across the realms long before any of us.
Those luminescent stones are the real hoard. The dragon is only the lock on the chest.
Dragons drop nothing but coin, or so the bitter ones say.
I heard dragons talk to your corpse after they kill you. Not sure I want to know what they say.
Some swear killing the big giants nearby takes a dragon's fire away. I swear they are drunk.
A dragon is just a big lizard until it breathes on you. Then it is a religion.
Dragon lairs smell of old coin and bad decisions.
I asked a town guard about the dragon once. He told me to go home. Very helpful.
Heard the three dragons dream about each other. A Bard probably made that up, but I like it.
Legend says the first group to find a dragon was a lost explorer who took a wrong turn.
Ask an Alb and their dragon is the oldest. Ask anyone else and you get two more answers.
I remember when nobody knew the dragons existed, until some fool wandered into a lair.
Each frontier has an old giant that belongs to no realm: a Green Knight, a Glacier Giant and Evern. Walk around them.
The Green Knight leaves you alone unless you start it. Wise people keep riding.
The con colours lie. I once saw an orange gut a full group.
Never trust a con on anything with a name. The colour is a mood, not a level.
Purple is purple. There is no colour for run now, and there should be.
My theory is the con colours were set by someone who never pulled anything.
Blue cons have killed more of us than reds ever did. Nobody respects a blue.
Never say the item's name in chat while you camp it. My old guild swore the mob hears.
Old wisdom says drops improve the moment the whole camp stops talking about them.
I keep a lucky ring in my pack for rare drops. It has not worked once. Still will not sell it.
Dragon scales would make amazing armor, if only someone would let crafters near one.
The stealth folk claim drops come better if you open from behind. Of course they would.
A healer friend never loots first. Says the luck follows whoever was humble.
Never camp one spot too long after dark. Old superstition says the camp starts noticing.
The islands just turned up one autumn, as if they had always been there. Bet there are more.
Every realm has a story about a pass that came out of the mist one day where no pass had been.
There is always one more dungeon nobody has found yet. Always.
Every year someone finds a new cave and everyone acts surprised. I stopped being surprised.
I bet the world goes further than any map they sell.
The old maps show roads that are not there any more. Either the mapmaker was drunk or the world moved.
I still keep a first map with half the coast missing. It was more honest.
The old maps had whole stretches marked unknown. Best part of the map.
Half the fun early on was not knowing what was over the next hill.
Nobody charted the far corners properly. I swear there are caves nobody mentions.
I keep a journal of spots I stumbled into that show up on no map.
Every realm has a tale about a lost place that the older maps almost show.
Some sages say the gods are still drawing the world, one island at a time.
The Bards claim the land was half the size at the start, and it grows a little each year.
Heard there is a vendor out in the wilds who sells maps of places that do not exist yet.
When I see a ledge nobody talks about, in I go. Usually it is just a bear.
Found a ruined wall once that nobody could name. Still wondering whose it was.
Every ridge looks climbable right up until you slide back down.
I could swear the fog out past the coast moves when nobody is looking.
Real explorers never ask directions. We get lost on purpose.
Best kind of evening: no group, no plans, just riding toward a coastline nobody bothered with.
I still wonder who carved the old markers out in the wilds. Half of them point at nothing.
An old hunter swore the wild beasts remember the old roads the maps forgot.
Every map ends in water, but the water does not end. Swim far enough and you hit the wall the gods put there.
I once swam out until the water went dark. Then nothing, just a wall you cannot see.
Heard if you swim far enough out the fog gets thicker, and then there is just a wall.
A friend swam to the edge of the world and came back saying the sky just stops.
I think the wall at the edge is there to keep something out, not to keep us in.
The edge of the world is real, I swam into it. Like cold glass under the sea.
Nobody can say what is beyond the wall. I asked a sage once, he told me to go level.
A swim to the edge takes forever. Bring patience, the view is worth it.
Heard there is an island out past the last map's edge that you can see but never reach.
I dare anyone to swim to the edge in full plate and back.
One day I will swim to the edge with no speed buff, just to say I did.
Every dungeon has a room behind the room. Never found one myself, but I check every wall.
Heard there is a wall in one of the old dungeons that only opens when nobody is watching.
I once walked along every wall of a dungeon hunting a secret door. All I found was a rat.
Some corners in the old dungeons look built for something that never moved in. Gives me chills.
An old Bard told me every crypt has one sealed room nobody opens. I half believe it.
Heard of a Bard who dragged a whole camp across a zone and lived. Probably a lie.
You hear about healers who never died once all the way to fifty. Nobody I know has met one.
Old raid leaders turn into legends faster than the dragons do.
Word is the imps know every rumour in all three realms. I should ask them.
The best part of a good legend is that nobody can prove anything.
Heard the old gods still walk the roads now and then. I wave at every stranger.
Nothing beats a good ghost story at the bind stone.
Six relics, two per realm. There were supposed to be more. I keep wondering where they are.
I think the missing relics are buried out there, waiting for someone to stumble on them.
Some say the other relics were never made. I like the version where they sit in a chest somewhere.
Every realm guards two relics and swears its pair is the oldest.
Albs have their lost city, Mids have their lost hall, Hibs have their door under the hill. Everyone has a place they cannot find.
Every realm swears its legends are the oldest. I think all three are right.
Legends never die, they just grow another verse each time a Bard sings them.
Half of lore is people who wiped explaining why.
The battlegrounds have their own ghosts too. Every one has a hill where someone stood against ten.
Heard a renegade chieftain in the battlegrounds remembers every face that ever beat him.
Dragon raids are three hours of standing around for a stone. I will level instead.
Legion lore is fun, but lore never gave anyone a bubble.
I dare someone to run up to Behemoth just to wave. Once.
Someday I will stand where Legion can see me and not run. Someday.
